_join_shaping_why: Measured on all five bank specs with check-join-audibility.js (2026-10-09, probe runs on the voice track only): the raw builds scored 30-46 dB at beat onsets against a ~25 dB 99th percentile because every beat starts after exact digital zeros -- the checker ignores zero frames, so what it measured was the 48k->8k resampler's pre-ringing (-88..-98 dB) next to a synthesized consonant. Four things fixed it TOGETHER, each measured: trim the lead-in to the first 1ms block over -45 dB (bank-03 join 5 needed the block, not a single sample), ramp the onset over 50 ms from a 0.07 gain floor (a fade from zero scored 39-65 dB; a 0.15 floor left a plosive 'But' at 29 dB), and a -63 dB RMS pink room-tone bed so no frame is ever exact zero (what a lav mic gives Heath's own takes). Result: 0 of 5/6/5/6/5 joins above p99 on specs 01-05. Same four values on every bank spec.

beats.text: If you are buying in Bernie this month, the September numbers just handed you leverage.

Fifty Bernie homes closed in September. Average sale price, six hundred twenty five thousand. Average days on market, one hundred seven. And the average seller took ninety six cents on the dollar against list.
San Antonio, same filters, same month. Three hundred thirty seven thousand average, ninety six days, ninety nine cents on the dollar.
So San Antonio sellers are barely moving off list. Bernie sellers, on average, came down four percent. On a six hundred thousand dollar house, that four percent is twenty four thousand dollars.

But those numbers are averages, one month, fifty sales. A fresh listing in a hot pocket is not negotiating. A house sitting past a hundred days probably is. Ask your agent for days on market before you write an offer.
Comment DEADLINES and I will send you every date in the Texas contract, so the deal you just negotiated does not die on a missed day.
